item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains BACKLOG.md and the tasktracker package). Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria:

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for the new behaviour (including LIFO across kinds, id non-reuse after undoing an add, and failed ops not recorded); keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what this ticket needs. Make one commit containing only this ticket's work, with a clear message; do not push and do not change git identity.

pr.body:
Approach: TaskStore keeps an in-memory undo log of successful add/complete/delete entries. complete records the previous status; delete records the removed Task object; add records its id. undo() pops the last entry and reverses it. _next_id is never rolled back, so ids are not reused.

Key files: tasktracker/store.py (undo log, undo, _undo_add/_undo_complete/_undo_delete); tests/test_undo.py (11 new tests: NothingToUndo on empty, each kind's undo, delete restores same object and order, LIFO across kinds, id non-reuse, failed complete/delete/add not recorded).

Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -> 15 tests OK. No lint tool installed; stdlib only.

Assumptions and limits: undoing complete restores the previous status, so completing an already-done task and undoing it leaves it done. The undo log is unbounded and holds references to deleted tasks (review follow-up). Delete records the live object, so a caller mutating the object returned by delete() affects the restore (review follow-up). undo() dispatches unknown kinds as delete via a bare else (follow-up). No test covers restoring the due date (follow-up). Assertions in the undo helpers are stripped under python -O.
pr.summary: made TaskStore.undo() revert the latest add, complete or delete, LIFO across kinds. now can roll back task changes; ids stay unique after undoing an add. before: no undo, now: undo() raises NothingToUndo when nothing is left. failed ops are not recorded.
pr.title: TT-104: add undo to TaskStore

agt_01M88XW8Q3XYFHRSAR7VD2HGVQ:1.description: The undo log is unbounded and holds references to every added, completed and deleted task, so memory grows with every mutation in a long-lived store. A cap or a documented limit is a possible follow-up. at tasktracker/store.py:16

agt_01M88XW8Q3XYFHRSAR7VD2HGVQ:2.description: The delete entry stores the live Task object. If a caller mutates the object returned by delete(), undo restores that mutated state rather than the state at delete time. Snapshotting on delete would make the restore exact. at tasktracker/store.py:42

agt_01M88XW8Q3XYFHRSAR7VD2HGVQ:3.description: undo() dispatches with a bare else, so any unknown kind is treated as delete. An explicit elif kind == 'delete' with a fallback raise would make failures visible. at tasktracker/store.py:45

agt_01M88XW8Q3XYFHRSAR7VD2HGVQ:4.description: No test checks that undoing a delete restores the due date; the restore test only checks title, tags and status. at tests/test_undo.py:36

risk.why: Contained behaviour change in one in-memory class; no persistence format or deletion semantics change. Every add/complete/delete now appends to an unbounded log. Reviewer confirmed medium.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains BACKLOG.md and the tasktracker package). Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria:

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for the new behaviour; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what this ticket needs. Make one commit containing only this ticket's work, with a clear message; do not push and do not change git identity.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains BACKLOG.md and the tasktracker package). Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria:

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for the new behaviour (including titles with commas, quotes, newlines, and empty tags/due); keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what this ticket needs. Make one commit containing only this ticket's work, with a clear message; do not push and do not change git identity.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog (contains BACKLOG.md and the tasktracker package). Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md exactly, following its acceptance criteria:

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates (`2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`). Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for the new behaviour; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Change only what this ticket needs. Make one commit containing only this ticket's work, with a clear message; do not push and do not change git identity.
